decisions.reason: The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY capturing the strong, frothy target texture; the source Requirement's motor and whisk evaluation criteria require no additional candidate-state change.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY capturing easy cleaning or removal of the bowls; the BOM motor and whisk criteria add no further removal-and-swap change.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already captures the solenoid valve, mix-open-pour sequence, and controlled non-sputtering flow, while no-dripping behavior was already present.
The candidate already has a same-message MODIFY capturing minimal splashing and the optional splash guard or bowl lip.
Requesting evaluation of motor speed and alternative whisk materials does not change the existing V1 sourcing policy or its established custom-spout exception.
The source decision does not change the spout's location, orientation, appearance, or construction; its solenoid and flow clauses concern dispensing operation instead.
The component-evaluation criteria do not change the system-layout deliverable or the selected CAD design direction.
The client requests input on component choices but does not change the requirement to provide a basic wiring plan.
The client asks the BOM owner to evaluate alternative whisk heads but does not select a replacement or cancel the existing whisk size, compatibility, or style constraints.
The source does not change bowl capacity or form; bowl cleaning and removability are independently represented by the removal-and-swap Requirement.
The motor and whisk evaluation criteria do not alter the DJ-turntable-inspired visual identity.
The source reiterates that spout components should be easy to clean or removable, which is already entailed by the candidate's existing removable-or-flushable cleaning method.
